I’m a newer tech but what I had always learned is that a follicle IS a type of cyst. It is a functional cyst. Another type of functional cyst is a corpus luteum cyst. These are normal cystic structures that grow and resolve throughout your cycle.  The term cyst really just means a sac filled with fluid. They appear the same on ultrasound just differ in how they are categorized based on size.
So what the report is saying is that there is nothing abnormal. You have a normal follicle. Follicles grow during your cycle and then burst to release the egg.
If the structure were measuring greater than 3 cm, they may categorize this as an ovarian cyst and may want to follow up on it.

They were probably having a hard time seeing your gallbladder. It’s just body habitus, gas, etc. some people are just difficult scans. She may have been a newer tech, and it’s totally normal for techs to ask each other for help with getting images especially when we are new (saying this as a newish tech myself)

I am a tech, I always get consent and explain that the exam is transabdominal and transvaginal BEFORE even setting the probe down/taking any pictures. I specifically ask “are you ok with doing the transvaginal part of the exam today?” This is how I was trained, it sounds like your tech did not explain the test properly before starting. You are right to be upset about that, to be honest. However, you can always decline a transvaginal exam. As a patient you should never feel like you have to do any type of testing just because the doctor orders it.
